Q: curl error message "Object of class stdClass could not be converted to string" when using google computeRoute A:

The value of CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS is mixed as you correctly identified. See here and here. So, when should it be a string and when should it be an array. The docs describes this:

The full data to post in a HTTP POST operation. This parameter can either be passed as a urlencoded string like 'para1=val1&para2=val2&...' or as an array with the field name as key and field data as value. If value is an array, the Content-Type header will be set to multipart/form-data. Files can be sent using CURLFile or CURLStringFile, in which case value must be an array. Available as of cURL 7.1.0. So, let's see your content-type header:

'Content-Type: application/json',

Since it's JSON, not multiplart/form-data, you will need to pass a String. So you should not decode your JSON via

CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS =>   json_decode(json_encode($this->converToObjects())),

especially not to an Std object. Whenever you need an array, pass true as a second parameter to json_decode, see here, but in your case you simply need to encode the JSON, via

CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS =>   json_encode($this->converToObjects()),

Q: Combining to tables for all possible options A:

An alternate approach using ADO to join the two sets of values:

Sub CombineTablesADO()
    Dim cn As Object, rs As Object, wbPath As String
    
    wbPath = ThisWorkbook.FullName 'path to the workbook
    
    Set cn = CreateObject("ADODB.Connection")
    cn.Open "Provider=Microsoft.ACE.OLEDB.12.0;Data Source=" & wbPath & _
            ";Extended Properties=""Excel 12.0;HDR=Yes;IMEX=1"";"
    
    'query and combine the two lists:
    
    'using sheet+range
    Set rs = cn.Execute("select a.*, b.* from [Sheet1$A1:A10] a,[Sheet1$B1:B10] b")

    '...or using named ranges "LISTA" and "LISTB"
    Set rs = cn.Execute("select a.*, b.* from [LISTA] a,[LISTB] b")
    
    'place the results on the worksheet
    ThisWorkbook.Worksheets("Sheet1").Range("D1").CopyFromRecordset rs
End Sub

Q: API that provides a list of stock names given a sector name A:

Alpha Vantage is relevant for sector-based analysis, but it does not directly provide a simple API call to list all stocks in a sector. Instead, it offers aSECTORfunction that returns real-time and historical performance data for 11 S&P 500 sectors.

To get specific stock tickers, use the SYMBOL_SEARCH function with keywords or rely on external, comprehensive stock market lists (such as listing files from NASDAQ/NYSE) to map tickers to sectors.
